A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAGE/SAGE-RL study and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Appendices A–D correspond across versions; v4 adds Appendix E.

before.justification: v1 reports original decoding and reinforcement-learning experiments, mathematical benchmark evaluations, ablations, reasoning-behavior analyses, and timing results in Sections 4–7 and Appendices B–D.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and their outcomes, including the benchmark results in Tables 1–5 and the appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The proposed TSearch exploration, SAGE stepwise sampling and termination, and SAGE-RL mixed rollouts remain unchanged in Sections 3, 5, and 6. Appendix E supplies illustrative implementation code rather than establishing a revised method.

E1.justification: Both versions use English DAPO and MATH level 3–5 training problems and evaluate MATH-500, AIME 2024, AIME 2025, AMC23, OlympiadBench, and Minerva. No new task, domain, population, or test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 4 retain the same per-model comparator rows for LC-R1, ThinkPrune-2k, AdaptThink, Efficient Reasoning, GRPO-LEAD, GRPO, and GSPO. Table 3 retains greedy sampling, random sampling, and beam search. Newly cited works are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: The model configurations, sampled subsets, metrics, and experimental settings are retained. Appendix C.2 still specifies 600 training steps, group size eight with two SAGE rollouts, and evaluation at 32,768 tokens. Appendix E's example defaults do not establish changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: The exploration-width and termination-tolerance ablations, SAGE versus Degrade-SAGE comparisons, rollout-count sensitivity, difficulty-level analysis, RFCS analysis, and timing studies are unchanged. The two case studies are retained as Figures 19–20 instead of Figures 16–17.

E5.justification: Both versions report eight evaluation runs for MATH-500, Minerva, and OlympiadBench and 32 for the other benchmarks. Section 5.2's mean@4/mean@16 reporting and existing graphical uncertainty displays are also unchanged.

E6.justification: All five result tables and the existing plotted results and case studies are retained. For example, Table 2 reports DS-1.5B with SAGE-GRPO at 84.8% pass@1 and 2,915 response tokens on MATH-500 in both versions.

T1.justification: The RFCS definition, scoring and search equations, GRPO/GSPO objectives in Appendix C.1, and complexity reasoning in Appendix D.4 are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or formal derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: reasoning models implicitly know when to stop, SAGE exposes efficient reasoning paths, and SAGE-RL transfers these patterns into ordinary inference.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning confidence, exploration, training dynamics, difficult problems, and computational tradeoffs remain unchanged. Appendix D.1's discussion moves relative to Table 4 but does not introduce new explanations or limitations.

D1.justification: New Appendix E substantially expands implementation documentation through example Python code covering initialization, sampling parameters, stepwise exploration, candidate management, scoring, termination, and final-answer generation. v4 also adds a project-page pointer and implementation contact. The previously reported training and evaluation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to Lu et al. (2026) and Chen et al. (2026), plus an Appendix A.1 paragraph citing vision, representation-learning, and normalization work. The paper's central positioning against existing efficient-reasoning approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 corrects the template running header, revises author order and affiliation/contribution information, and adds Appendix E and a related-work paragraph. The existing scientific prose and section organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds three syntax-highlighted code displays as Figures 15–17, adjusts the title-page layout and Figure 1 sizing, and relocates Table 4 relative to its discussion. Existing experimental graphics are preserved; the final three figures are renumbered 18–20.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves usability through Appendix E's explicit implementation flow, project/contact information, and corrected headers. Scientific support remains unchanged. The documentation gain is limited by an unresolved inconsistency: Figure 17 normalizes scores using a token count that includes the prompt, whereas Equation 1 defines normalization over generated tokens. The appendix therefore helps explain implementation without fully resolving reproducibility.
